entries.title: Psalms 119:1
segments:
This is an alphabetic psalm of peculiar structure.  The first eight verses begin each with the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, the next eight with the second letter, and so on.  It is wholly occupied with the commendation of God's word under various titles, expressive of the various aspects in which it may be viewed.  Thus it is called his word, as that which he has spoken to us; his law, given as the rule of our life; his commandments and precepts, laid upon us to be kept; his statutes, established as the laws of his kingdom; his judgments, as his decisions concerning our duty and destiny; his testamonies, as to his authoritative declaration of truth; and his way, in which we are to walk. 
 
  Undefiled; sincere, upright. 
 
  In the law; according to its requirements.

entries.title: Psalms 119:3
segments:
Do no iniquity; allow themselves in no known sin. 
 
The best way to be kept from all iniquity is to be diligently employed in learning and doing the whole will of God.

entries.title: Psalms 119:6
segments: They who have respect to all God's commandments have the approbation of conscience, and their hope shall never be disappointed.

entries.title: Psalms 119:9
segments:
Taking heed; regulating his life according to the Scriptures. 
 
He who takes the Bible for his guide will walk in safety, purity, and love; and will be preserved from manifold dangers to which he would otherwise be exposed.

entries.title: Psalms 119:11
segments: Hid; as a precious treasure to be carefully kept.

entries.title: Psalms 119:15
segments: Meditation upon the word and ways of God is a great safeguard to youth, and to those of riper years.

entries.title: Psalms 119:18
segments: The mind needs to be spiritually enlightened in order to behold the spiritual meaning, beauty, and excellence of the Scriptures.

entries.title: Psalms 119:19
segments: A stranger in the earth; as a stranger has no inheritance in the land of his pilgrimage, so I am as a stranger on the earth, having no inheritance but thy word.  Therefore take not away from me this precious treasure, but let it be before my eyes continually as my comforter,

entries.title: Psalms 119:24
segments: Those who take counsel of the statutes of God will be likely to be made wise to salvation.

entries.title: Psalms 119:25
segments: Cleaveth unto the dust; lies prostrate; a description of deep depression.

entries.title: Psalms 119:26
segments:
Have declared; recounted before thee. 
 
  My ways; my goings out and comings in; my whole course of life, with all its cares and sorrows.

entries.title: Psalms 119:28
segments: Melteth; pineth away.

entries.title: Psalms 119:30
segments: Men must make their duty their delight, or they will not be likely to perform it.

entries.title: Psalms 119:37
segments:
Beholding; beholding with delight. 
 
  Vanity; put here for all the vain objects of time and sense to which men look, instead of God, for happiness.

entries.title: Psalms 119:43
segments: Take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; deal not with me in such a way that I shall be unable to glory in thy word of truth before my enemies, as I have done heretofore.

entries.title: Psalms 119:45
segments: At liberty; literally, in a wide place, where I can walk safely and prosperously.

entries.title: Psalms 119:46
segments: Those who love God will not be afraid to speak of him before the great and honorable of the earth.

entries.title: Psalms 119:48
segments: My hands also will I lift up; as a token of affectionate desire.

entries.title: Psalms 119:49
segments: The word; the word of promise.

entries.title: Psalms 119:50
segments: This; trust in thy word of promise.

entries.title: Psalms 119:53
segments:
Horror; vehement disapprobation. 
 
Pious men are grieved when the wicked break God's law.

entries.title: Psalms 119:55
segments: Serious thought and contemplation on the works and ways of God, and on our relations to him and obligations to obey him, are essential to the hearty turning of the soul to his service.

entries.title: Psalms 119:56
segments: This I had; the comfort mentioned above,
.  But some render the verse thus: "This I have, that I keep thy precepts;" meaning, "This I have as my heritage, or the portion of my soul, that I keep thy precepts."  Compare

entries.title: Psalms 119:59
segments: My ways; comparing them with thy law.

entries.title: Psalms 119:61
segments: The bands of the wicked have robbed me; or, the snares of the wicked have encompassed me.

entries.title: Psalms 119:64
segments: Full of thy mercy: teach; do thou, whose goodness fills the earth, show thy goodness to me by teaching me thy statutes.  Compare Ps 119.58.

entries.title: Psalms 119:67
segments: Afflictions are often made the means of reclaiming the soul from backsliding, and thus promoting its highest good.s

entries.title: Psalms 119:70
segments: Fat; pampered in worldly pleasures, and insensible to spiritual goods.

entries.title: Psalms 119:72
segments: No earthly good is so precious or useful as the keeping of the divine commands.

entries.title: Psalms 119:74
segments: The deliverance of a pious soul from trouble gives great joy to the people of God.

entries.title: Psalms 119:79
segments: Turn unto me; in love and confidence.  This is the effect of the witnessing God's bountiful dealings with him.

entries.title: Psalms 119:82
segments: Fail for thy word; pine away in looking for the fulfilment of thy word of promise.

entries.title: Psalms 119:83
segments:
Bottle in the smoke; dried up and withered. 
 
By great and long-continued afflictions the soul may be deprived of rest, peace, and joy; yet it will still cleave to God's service.

entries.title: Psalms 119:84
segments: How many are the days of thy servant? the meaning of this question in the original seems to be, To what do his days amount?  He pleads the shortness of life as a reason why God should speedily deliver him. Compare

entries.title: Psalms 119:88
segments: The effect of God's grace bestowed upon the righteous is an increase of the fruits of obedience.

entries.title: Psalms 119:89
segments: Settled in heaven; established in God's presence beyond the possibility of change.

entries.title: Psalms 119:90
segments: Abideth; remaineth unmoved.  The stability of the earth is the effect of God's unchangeableness, and the same unchangeableness is shown in the fulfilment of his word.

entries.title: Psalms 119:96
segments:
An end of all perfection; of himan excellence. 
 
  Exceeding broad; searching the heart and motives, and requiring every thing that is excellent. 
 
Nothing merely human is perfect; perfection is attained only by perfect obedience to the revealed will of God.

entries.title: Psalms 119:103
segments: The law of God is the delight of his people, and shows them the path of duty, safety, and blessedness.

entries.title: Psalms 119:105
segments: A lamp unto my feet; showing the way in which I should go.

entries.title: Psalms 119:109
segments: My soul is continually in my hand; my life is constantly in danger.

entries.title: Psalms 119:113
segments: Vain thoughts; the original word, which occurs only here, seems to denote divided, or inconstant thoughts, now inclining to obedience, and now to disobedience.  Compare

entries.title: Psalms 119:117
segments: The only safety of believers is in being kept by the mighty power of God through faith unto salvation.

entries.title: Psalms 119:122
segments: Be surety for thy servant for good; be surety for me, that in the cause between me and my adversaries I shall receive justice.  See note to

entries.title: Psalms 119:127
segments:
vv 127-128. 
 
  Therefore; because of the excellence of thy word, which the psalmist has been setting forth throughout the whole psalm.  See

entries.title: Psalms 119:130
segments:
The entrance of thy words; more literally, the opening of thy words, that is, the unfolding of Scripture to my soul through the illumination of thy Spirit. 
 
The reception of divine truth illuminates and purifies the soul.

entries.title: Psalms 119:147
segments:
I prevented the dawning of the morning; cried unto God during the night season and before the dawn of day. 
 
The way to the throne of mercy is always open, and God sees the wants of his people amidst the darkness of midnight, as well as in the splendors of noonday.

entries.title: Psalms 119:155
segments: Without seeking for the pearl of great price we shall not be likely to obtain it.

entries.title: Psalms 119:160
segments: Thy word is true from the beginning; or, the sum of thy word is true; that is, the whole of it taken as a body.

entries.title: Psalms 119:164
segments:
Seven times; many times, often. 
 
The righteous pray with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watch thereunto with all perseverance.

entries.title: Psalms 119:165
segments:
Nothing shall offend them; they shall have no stumbling-blocks, their way shall be safe and prosperous. 
 
Obedience to God's law is the only way of peace and safety.

entries.title: Psalms 119:168
segments: All my ways are before thee; thine omniscient eye is upon all my ways, so that if in any thing I depart from thy commands, thou seest it, and wilt treat me accordingly.

entries.title: Psalms 119:175
segments: Thy judgments; by which thou sustainest the righteous and overthrowest the wicked.  See above in

entries.title: Psalms 119:176
segments: Gone astray; wandered from the fold, and thus become exposed to misery and ruin.
